newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA SAFCOL PRIVATISATION TALKS TO RESUME SOON.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA SAFCOL PRIVATISATION TALKS TO RESUME SOON.

text.p: Discussions between the Public Enterprises Ministry and the South African Forestry Co (Safcol) on the state-owned firm's restructuring would begin within the next few days, a ministry spokesman said on Friday.
Safcol is one of seven public sector corporations Minister Stella Sigcau said late last month would be at least partly privatised by the end of 1997.
"They will meet within the next few days. It is a matter of co-ordinating the diaries of the minister and the management of Safcol," ministry spokesman Wandile Zote told Reuters.
He said various restructuring options for Safcol would be discussed.

Moves to restructure Safcol were halted last year by Water Affairs and Forestry Minister Kader Asmal who said it was necessary to first establish how the former homeland forests, which government holds as a separate asset to the timber firm, would be dealt with.
Government has been criticised for its lack of progress in privatising state-owned assets, a key component of its macro-economic package unveiled in June last year.

State groups which are to be fully privatised are domestic airline Sun Air, whose privatisation advisers were announced earlier this month, tourist resort group Aventura, mining group Alexcor and transport group Autonet.
Strategic equity stakes are to be sold in telecommunications utility Telkom, the Airports Company which runs South Africa's major airports and Safcol.
